# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
## 40,000 Users — Legacy → New Billing System (Dual-Run Supported)

## Overview

Both billing systems can run concurrently, so this plan uses a phased, cohort-based migration with dual-write/dual-run reconciliation rather than a hard cutover. The old system remains live and authoritative for unmigrated users throughout all phases and is only addressed for decommissioning after 100% of users are confirmed stable on the new system.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (Internal + Opt-In Low-Risk Users)

**Scope:** 1% of users (~400 accounts)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including a full reconciliation dry-run against a production data snapshot with zero unexplained discrepancies, and rollback tooling has been tested successfully at least once in a rehearsal.

**Composition:** Internal test accounts, employees, and opted-in low-ARPU users on simple (non-multi-currency, non-enterprise-contract) plans.

**Duration:** Minimum 5 business days.

**Actions:**
- Migrate accounts with dual-write to both systems.
- Run automated daily reconciliation of invoices, balances, and payment events between old and new systems.
- Manually review 100% of billing events for this cohort.

**Exit criterion:** Invoice/payment discrepancy rate < 0.1%, zero P1 incidents, support ticket volume for migrated cohort within 1.5x baseline.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (Representative Sample)

**Scope:** 15% of users (~6,000 accounts, cumulative)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met and signed off by Billing Engineering Lead and Customer Support Lead; no open P1/P2 defects in the migration pipeline.

**Composition:** Randomized, stratified sample covering all plan types, geographies, currencies, and payment methods to surface edge cases before broad exposure.

**Duration:** Minimum 10 business days.

**Actions:**
- Automate reconciliation reporting (hourly, not just daily).
- Enable customer-facing new billing portal for this cohort behind a feature flag.
- Load-test new system at 3x this cohort's peak transaction volume.

**Exit criterion:** Payment failure rate delta vs. old system < 0.2 percentage points, reconciliation discrepancy rate < 0.05%, support escalation rate stable or declining.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (Majority Rollout)

**Scope:** 60% of users (~24,000 accounts, cumulative ~75%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met; finance has reconciled a full monthly billing cycle end-to-end for the Phase 2 cohort with no material variance; customer support has completed training and runbooks for new-system issues.

**Composition:** Remaining standard accounts, migrated in daily waves of no more than 10% of total users per day to preserve rollback granularity.

**Duration:** Minimum 15 business days.

**Actions:**
- Migrate in daily sub-batches with automated go/no-go checks before each batch.
- Maintain dual-run reconciliation continuously.
- Begin customer communications about the upcoming full cutover.

**Exit criterion:** Cumulative discrepancy rate < 0.05% sustained for 10 consecutive days; zero unresolved P1 incidents.

---

## Phase 4: Final Migration (Remaining Users, Including High-Complexity Accounts)

**Scope:** Final 24% of users (~9,600 accounts; enterprise contracts, multi-currency, custom billing arrangements, legal holds)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 exit criteria met; each remaining high-complexity account has an individually reviewed migration plan signed off by both Billing Engineering and Account Management; a fallback path to the old system remains fully operational and tested.

**Duration:** Minimum 15 business days, with high-touch accounts migrated in the smallest sub-batches (≤500/day).

**Actions:**
- White-glove migration for enterprise/complex accounts with dedicated support contact.
- Full parallel run (old system continues processing in shadow mode) for at least one full billing cycle post-migration for this cohort.
- No changes to the old system's availability during this phase — it remains fully active in shadow/fallback mode.

**Exit criterion:** All 40,000 users migrated; one full billing cycle reconciled with < 0.05% discrepancy; zero open P1 incidents.

---

## Phase 5: Old System Decommissioning

**Scope:** N/A (infrastructure phase, no user migration activity)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 4 exit criteria met, all 40,000 users successfully migrated and stable for at least one full billing cycle, finance sign-off on final reconciliation, and a minimum 30-day cooling-off period with the old system in read-only/shadow mode.

**Actions:**
- Move old system to read-only mode, then archive data per retention policy.
- Decommission old system infrastructure only after archival is verified restorable.

*Note: This decommissioning phase is intentionally separated from Phase 4 (final batch of user migration) to avoid removing the fallback path before the last and highest-risk cohort has proven stable.*

---

## Risks

RISK: Reconciliation logic itself has a defect, masking real discrepancies as false negatives | Independently validate reconciliation code via a second team; inject known synthetic discrepancies into a test batch to confirm detection | QA Lead
RISK: Duplicate or missed charges during dual-write due to race conditions between old and new systems | Implement idempotency keys on all payment operations and a single source-of-truth ledger flag per account during transition | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: High-complexity enterprise accounts (multi-currency, custom contracts) break in ways not caught by earlier phases | Hold all such accounts for Phase 4 white-glove migration with individual sign-off and dedicated rollback plan per account | Account Management Lead
RISK: Customer confusion or trust erosion from visible billing discrepancies during migration | Proactive customer communications before each phase, dedicated support queue for migration-related tickets, credit/goodwill policy for confirmed errors | Customer Support Lead
RISK: Migration tooling or scripts fail partway through a batch, leaving accounts in an inconsistent state | Build idempotent, resumable migration scripts with automatic per-account rollback on partial failure; test resumability in staging before each phase | Platform/DevOps Lead
RISK: Regulatory/compliance exposure from incorrect tax or invoice data in a jurisdiction not covered by test data | Include compliance/legal review of tax and invoice formatting per jurisdiction before Phase 2 expansion, with region-specific spot checks | Compliance Lead

---

## Halt Criteria (Automated Circuit Breaker)

The rollout must be automatically paused and no further accounts migrated if, at any point during a phase:

- **Billing discrepancy rate exceeds 0.5%** of migrated accounts' transactions in any rolling 24-hour window, OR
- Payment failure rate for migrated cohort exceeds old-system baseline by more than 1 percentage point, OR
- Any single P1 incident (e.g., duplicate charges, failed payment processing affecting >100 accounts) occurs.

On halt: freeze further migrations, do not roll back already-migrated accounts unless data integrity is compromised, convene incident review within 4 hours, and require explicit sign-off from Billing Engineering Lead and Customer Support Lead to resume.

---

PHASES: 5
